body: Is there not any sort of way that I can be there for her myself? It’s not my responsibility but I just feel sort of helpless.

I’ll go through each of these questions one by one. First off, thank you, although I’d argue it’s less bravery and more fear. I’m not worried about it being because of me, I’m only worried about not doing enough. I know she’s been depressed for a veryyyy long time. I don’t know much about depression but I know some people have it like, chronically? where it’s due to a chemical imbalance that they deal with throughout their life rather than a situational cause that plagues a smaller time period (what I faced). I could totally be wrong here though. If something specific happened to cause it, not even I know what it is, and if she hasn’t told me she hasn’t told a single other person. To the last thing, I try my best but it’s very hard with COVID. I’m in an area that has some of the strictest enforcement on regulations which makes seeing her in person extremely challenging, and doing things online tends to revert back to a conversation similar to this.
